haiku-low.q1: Pages of up to 500 products ordered by id ascending, fetched one at a time on Wi-Fi only; never in parallel.
haiku-low.q2: In sync_state as cursor, the last product id of the last fully saved page, written in the same transaction as the page insert into products_staging.
haiku-low.q3: Catch-up replays every change after catchup_seq (starting at start_seq) into staging, using change_seq so newer versions and deletes are applied correctly.
haiku-low.q4: The server returns 410 resync_required, and the client starts a full download again; existing products stay visible until the swap.
haiku-low.q5: Staging is emptied, cursor cleared, new start_seq taken, and it is built in products_staging. It becomes live in the swap transaction that drops products and renames staging.
haiku-low.q6: App launch and each return to foreground, on any network, only when phase is idle; at most once every 15 minutes.
haiku-low.q7: It repeats the same request after waiting 2s, 4s, 8s and 16s, at most 5 attempts total, then waits for the next trigger; saved state is kept.
haiku-low.q8: The current page finishes, then the download pauses until Wi-Fi returns. Incremental sync is unaffected.
haiku-low.q9: It skips the change if the stored row already has an equal or higher change_seq; otherwise it applies it.
haiku-low.q10: It starts from last_seq in sync_state. last_seq moves to next_seq in the same transaction as each applied page.
haiku-low.q11: It reads products stamped with change_seq from a global sequence at insert, update or delete. Deletes are rows with deleted=true, kept 7 days.

sonnet.q1: Keyset pagination: GET /catalogue/full?after_id=<cursor> returns up to 500 non-deleted products ordered by product id ascending, with done:true when none remain. Pages are fetched one at a time, never in parallel.
sonnet.q2: In the sync_state row's cursor (id of last product in last fully saved page). Each page is inserted into products_staging and the cursor updated in one SQLite transaction, so both are saved together or not at all.
sonnet.q3: start_seq (highest committed change_seq) is recorded at start; after the download finishes, step 4 catch-up replays /catalogue/changes after start_seq (tracked via catchup_seq) into staging, including new products with ids below the cursor and deletes. Skip rule avoids overwriting newer staged rows. Changes after the last catch-up page arrive via incremental sync after the swap.
sonnet.q4: The server returns 410 resync_required. The client goes back to step 2 and does a new full download (new start_seq, staging emptied, cursor cleared); products and last_seq are untouched so reps keep the existing catalogue.
sonnet.q5: It is built in products_staging (emptied, new start_seq, cursor cleared, phase=downloading), then caught up. It becomes the one the app reads at the step 5 swap: in one transaction drop products, rename products_staging to products, create new empty staging, set last_seq=catchup_seq, clear last_incremental_at, phase=idle. Until commit, reps see the old products.
sonnet.q6: App launch and return to foreground, only when phase = idle, on any network, at most once every 15 minutes (measured from last_incremental_at). If last_incremental_at is empty (after a swap or an interrupted sync), it runs without waiting.
sonnet.q7: Repeat the same request, waiting 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s: at most 5 attempts total. After the 5th failure it stops and waits for the next trigger, keeping everything already saved. Other 4xx are not retried (except 410).
sonnet.q8: The current page finishes, then the download pauses; it resumes when Wi-Fi returns (a trigger while phase = downloading). Incremental sync is unaffected.
sonnet.q9: Skip rule: skip the change if the stored row already has an equal or higher change_seq; otherwise apply it (upsert if not deleted, delete if deleted).
sonnet.q10: It starts from last_seq (GET /catalogue/changes?after_seq=<last_seq>). last_seq is set to next_seq in the same transaction that applies each page, so it advances per committed page.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED for what the server reads (the document says only that change_seq is stamped on product rows in Postgres and tombstone rows are kept 7 days). Deletes: represented as a change with the product id, its change_seq and deleted = true, backed by tombstone rows (deleted = true) kept 7 days then purged.
